text:
[IRET.11.3.5] **The edge-once set.** A clock-driven match — a token that
joins `$ClockTick` for a time-dependent test ([IRET.19.5]) — is formed again on
every tick, with a new token. Each terminal keeps a set of the fact ids whose
clock-driven match has fired. A re-formed activation for a fact in the set is
suppressed, tick after tick, until the match ends: the engine must remove the
fact's id when the time-dependent test goes false, so that the next true is a
new match and fires ([LTIM.2.5.1]), and when the fact leaves working memory. A
fact that is upserted takes a new id, which the set does not hold. Unlike the
table ([IRET.11.3]), the set survives a generation's turnover.

idris.name: ltim_2_4_3__retime_at_entry
idris.note: THE EDGE-ONCE SET IS THE `fired` FLAG here: a match the re-time leaves in place is one activation, its flag kept, so it is not fired again tick after tick; a test that goes false ends it, and a fact that is replaced takes a new id and a new stamp, a new match. LESS than the clause: no per-terminal set and no re-formed token, since there is no tick fact to join.
